iconicAnchor.label: Dieter Roth's concrete poetry and ideograms
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Dieter Roth and the postwar Concrete Poetry movement
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: MoMA describes concrete poetry as language whose placement receives the same attention as meaning and sound, with letters becoming abstract compositional material.

sources.title: Dieter Roth: The Concrete
supports: Concrete poetry gives spatial presentation equal weight with language, sound, and syncopation.
Roth's ideograms support treating language parts as visual elements arranged for compositional value.

sources.title: A throw of the dice
supports: Mallarme's spatial typography demonstrates how line placement, type size, and spread structure can carry meaning.
Broodthaers's transformation of text into black bars supports the guide's distinction between language and image.
